status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should provide meaningful information making stakeholders aware of interactions with AI, including workplace interactions.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Section 1.3(ii) is a nonbinding comparative AI-awareness benchmark for actors creating or using synthetic executive portrayals in the reported 2025 interactions. The AI-mediated interaction and period are established; no binding or certified conformity claim is made.
previous_canonical_assessment.finding_basis: The police account describes real executives being impersonated through deepfake video to induce the transfer, with the victim discovering the scam only later. That deceptive interaction withheld meaningful awareness that the apparent executive presence was AI-mediated. This information finding is independently grounded in the interaction, not inferred automatically from the economic/social-engineering taxonomy roles.

review.reason_for_change: The AI-mediated executive video directly engages stakeholder awareness of interaction with AI. The police account describes real executives being impersonated to induce the transfer, with the victim discovering the scam later. Meaningful awareness was withheld in that interaction; this independently contradicts Section 1.3(ii), irrespective of voluntary status.

review.requirement_proposition: Protect vulnerable users, require specific consent for bounded deceptive styles, document emergent deception and define safeguard-failure protocols.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: A finance director at a multinational corporation was contacted by scammers impersonating senior company personnel and joined a Zoom video conference in which the company's chief executive officer and others were impersonated using deepfake techno… IEEE 7014.1-2026 applies to partner-based GPAI systems using emulated empathy in human-AI partnering contexts. These sources describe synthetic videos/advertisements impersonating real people, not an empathic AI partner interacting with a user; they also do not describe personal or emotional data collection by such a partner system. The required system context is absent.

review.reason_for_change: The requirement governs emulated-empathy partner-based GPAI systems and their vulnerable-user/deceptive-style safeguards. Human-orchestrated executive video impersonation does not establish a human-AI partnering/empathy system; a deepfake alone does not instantiate the technical scope.

review.requirement_proposition: Add intended purpose, nominal operator and responsible contact information to the public documentation.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: IEEE-7001 Table 2 level 3 (Add intended purpose, nominal operator and responsible contact information to the public documentation.) requires a relevant ethical-design process/autonomous-system stakeholder level and conformance undertaking. The sources establish neither for the the March 2025 executive-impersonation transfer; only admitted metadata is used.

review.reason_for_change: Table 2 level 3 governs public documentation of an autonomous system's purpose, operator and responsible contact. The human-orchestrated deepfake impersonation does not establish that autonomous-system documentation object. Exclusion is technical scope, not unknown conformance.

review.requirement_proposition: Parties must ensure adequate transparency requirements tailored to the context and risk of AI lifecycle activities, including identification of AI-generated content.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Article 8 governs Parties and implemented territorial rights/transparency duties. Relevant entry into force, implementation covering the private actor and trigger are not established; fraud or police recovery alone supplies no treaty applicability.

review.reason_for_change: Article 8 imposes transparency requirements on treaty Parties through their lifecycle implementation duties. This March 2025 private scam in Singapore/Hong Kong does not fall within a commenced Convention duty for a relevant Party/territory; the provision is not a direct disclosure duty on the impersonators.

review.requirement_proposition: Make the system clearly identifiable as autonomous to users and bystanders.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: IEEE-7001 Table 2 level 1 (Make the system clearly identifiable as autonomous to users and bystanders.) requires a relevant ethical-design process/autonomous-system stakeholder level and conformance undertaking. The sources establish neither for the the March 2025 executive-impersonation transfer; only admitted metadata is used.

review.reason_for_change: Table 2 level 1 governs identifying an autonomous system to users and bystanders. Synthetic portrayals in a human-orchestrated video scam do not establish an autonomous system acting in that encounter. AI-generated media is not itself autonomy; the directly relevant OECD and NIST AI-interaction disclosure propositions are retained instead.

review.requirement_proposition: Parties must seek to ensure that people interacting with AI are told they are interacting with a system rather than a human, as appropriate to the context.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Article 15(2) governs Parties and implemented territorial rights/transparency duties. Relevant entry into force, implementation covering the private actor and trigger are not established; fraud or police recovery alone supplies no treaty applicability.

review.reason_for_change: Article 15(2) addresses a Party's assurance of AI-interaction notice. The March 2025 Singapore/Hong Kong scam does not instantiate a commenced treaty duty of the appropriate Party. Private deception does not automatically establish failure of a treaty-level implementation obligation.

review.requirement_proposition: Do not place, put into service or use AI that deploys subliminal, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques causing materially distorted behavior and significant harm.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: The Singapore/Hong Kong deepfake call led to a reported transfer exceeding US$499,000, but the record does not identify the generating system or establish an EU-market provider, Union-established deployer, or output used in the Union. The harm is material; the Article 2 connection needed to determine applicability is not established.

review.reason_for_change: Article 5(1)(a) concerns prohibited AI practices within the EU Act territorial actor scope. The March 2025 Singapore/Hong Kong interaction supplies no EU provider/deployer or Union output-use connection. Deceptive conduct elsewhere is not automatically an EU statutory occurrence finding.

review.requirement_proposition: Minimise data and make review, modification and withdrawal of consent immediate and accessible.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: A finance director at a multinational corporation was contacted by scammers impersonating senior company personnel and joined a Zoom video conference in which the company's chief executive officer and others were impersonated using deepfake techno… IEEE 7014.1-2026 applies to partner-based GPAI systems using emulated empathy in human-AI partnering contexts. These sources describe synthetic videos/advertisements impersonating real people, not an empathic AI partner interacting with a user; they also do not describe personal or emotional data collection by such a partner system. The required system context is absent.

review.reason_for_change: The requirement concerns data/consent controls in emulated-empathy partner-based GPAI systems collecting or retaining personal or relationship-history data. The reported scam establishes executive impersonation and a transfer, not this partnering-system data lifecycle.

review.requirement_proposition: Document interactions with GAI systems to users prior to interactive activities, particularly in contexts involving more significant risks.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: NIST-AI-600-1 GV-5.1-002 (Document interactions with GAI systems to users prior to interactive activities, particularly in contexts involving more significant risks.) is a voluntary organization/lifecycle action. The the March 2025 executive-impersonation transfer establishes no adoption or action-specific GAI/TEVV, risk, bias, assurance, disclosure or response programme. DNB’s procedure or pilot errors do not create that source-defined undertaking.

review.reason_for_change: The synthetic executive video was presented as a genuine executive interaction before the victim transferred funds. The police account establishes later discovery rather than advance disclosure. The specific NIST requirement to document GAI interaction to the user before interactive activity therefore did not hold in this bounded interaction; organisational framework adoption is not required.
